verdicts.reading: Global recorded-music performance-rights revenue would exceed $1 billion for the first time in 2014.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric against IFPI 2014 performance-rights revenue (within 10% hit).
verdicts.reason: IFPI's two vintages of 2014 performance-rights revenue disagree by about a factor of 2: about $948 million (+8.7%) in the Digital Music Report 2015, versus about $2 billion after IFPI widened the category in its 2016 report (both recalled; IFPI pages returned 404 or were blocked). D23: a spread above factor 2 is ungradable. Against the first vintage the forecast is 5% high (threshold not crossed); against the second it is crossed.

evidence.title: IFPI Digital Music Report 2015
evidence.shows: Source of the 2014 performance-rights figure (about $948m); file not retrievable in this session.

verdicts.reading: In 2014 mobile instant messaging would carry more than twice the daily volume of SMS (about 50 billion vs 21 billion messages a day).
verdicts.mainstream_test: Ratio test: MIM daily volume at least twice SMS daily volume in 2014 (the headline claim); the 50bn level is the stated estimate.
verdicts.reason: WhatsApp alone handled over 30 billion messages a day by early January 2015, against roughly 20 billion SMS a day; adding Facebook Messenger, WeChat, LINE, iMessage and others, MIM volume was well over twice SMS. Uncertain: if the 50bn figure is read as the claim, the total (likely well above 60bn, but no single measured series) would make it a miss or ungradable.

evidence.title: WhatsApp - Wikipedia
evidence.shows: Over 30 billion messages every day by early January 2015.

verdicts.reading: Nearly 220,000 3D printers, worth $1.6 billion, would be sold worldwide in 2015 (in line with Gartner's consensus).
verdicts.mainstream_test: D16 numeric on Gartner's 2015 worldwide 3D printer shipments (within 10% hit).
verdicts.reason: Gartner, the consensus Deloitte cites, forecast 217,350 for 2015 (October 2014) and later reported 2015 shipments of about 219,000 (recalled from its October 2016 release, which was blocked), within 1%. Wohlers' desktop counts are higher (about 278,000), so the median of estimates (about 245,000) would still be within about 10%. Low-to-moderate certainty on the actual.
